utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: Yes. Right away?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I guess private session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: We'd ask private session, Mr. President, out of caution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We will go to the private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Sorry, witness. Perhaps with my intervention, my confusion, I don't know if you got the question or not. Were some of you taken from Siroki Brijeg to Ljubuski around that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: Yes, seven or eight days later.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: And where were you held in Ljubuski?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: We were held -- I really don't know. We were led out of the bus. And under armed escort, we were taken to a place where there was wooden floors, terrible -- it was like in Siroki Brijeg. There was a professor there, sort of calculated that we each had 33 square centimetres of room per prisoner. So the conditions were terrible.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Witness CC, I'm not going to spend much time on Ljubuski. But is it correct you were only held there for a short time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Approximately two days?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: Two. Two, three days. And then 18 of us were returned to Siroki Brijeg.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: All right. Before going back to Siroki Brijeg, can you tell the Chamber a particular incident, if you recall, when someone came into the holding area at Ljubuski and took you to do some work or took you someplace else.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: I remember that Robo Medic came on one occasion. I was cutting wood at that time, and there were other people -- other prisoners who were there with me who were chopping that wood.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Were you able -- and I'll ask you why or how in a moment. But were you able to identify what unit, what military unit, this Robo Medic was from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: Yes, he was with the Convicts Battalion at Siroki Brijeg.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: How do you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: I know because I worked on a building that was being converted into a barracks. And in fact, they all bragged that they were members of the Convicts Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Did they mention the name -- did he or the others -- you just said "they." Did Mr. Medic or others identify their commander?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: Yes, they mentioned the name. They mentioned the name on several occasions because they would say, The boss ordered this and this, or, The general ordered this and that. And it was Mladen Naletilic, Tuta. They called him "Boss," "General," "Tuta."

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: You said you were taken back to Siroki Brijeg. What happened then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: When they brought us back to Siroki Brijeg, then the 18 of us were placed in those two cells. There was another prisoner.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Were you used to work any more after your return to Siroki Brijeg?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: Yes, we went to work every day.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Where did you work?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: We first worked at the swimming pool until we were done.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Was this the same swimming pool where you worked before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: Yes. But not everybody went to that pool. Because I personally went to Ivan's house to work while others went to work at the pool. I went with the others, too, at first, but then Ivan came and took me to his house to work there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: All right. Well, several questions coming out of that. But let me first stay at the swimming pool for a moment. Do you recall who any of the particular guards were or HVO soldiers that you were interacting with when you were on work detail, if you will, at the pool?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, I object to the form of that question. It assumes facts not in evidence. This witness has previously testified that the guards were the truck drivers. And now, my learned colleague is misstating the facts in stating HVO officers and soldiers, and this witness already testified it was only the truck drivers as guards. So I object to the form of the question, assuming facts not in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, is this the same time?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, this is the second occasion. I will rephrase the question, but there's no indication that it was the same people on the second date. That's my question. I'll rephrase the question, though.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Who were you guarded by at the time you were working at the pool the second time? The second series of times, who were you guarded or watched by?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: We were guarded by the same drivers, but now these drivers were in uniform and they were carrying weapons, which means that they were soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Can you remember the names of any particular of these soldiers or officers, and did you have any conversation or exchange with them in connection with working at the swimming pool?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: I remember that once when I was working, Zeljko Bosnjak came, and he took me to Tuta and he said, "This is the mujahedin from Cazin." He personally took me to Tuta and told Tuta, "Here is the mujahedin from Cazin," because I was the only one from Cazin. Tuta said that --

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: I'm going to interrupt you for a second. Sorry, Witness CC; my apology. I just want to give you a pause so the Judges hear your testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Just a moment. That's why I was talking to the President. You were talking about the few days that this witness had spent at Ljubuski, and then you began to talk about somebody called Robo Medic who came when they were cutting wood, but you never went back to that incident. We went back to the cells in Siroki Brijeg without elucidating that incident. Was that by intent or was it an accident?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Probably a little of both, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: If you don't want to go back, sorry for interrupting.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm trying to move quite efficiently, as best I can but perhaps you're absolutely right that it may be worth another answer or two.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Witness CC, let me take you back for a moment to this interaction with this man Medic. What did you do with him -- what further, if any, interaction did you have with him during the time that you were still in Ljubuski before being taken back to Siroki Brijeg?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: He drove a bus. He came to take -- to take us there by bus, and he took us to work at Siroki.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Essentially, he took -- you had some interaction with him and he took you, the group of you, back to Siroki Brijeg. Is that what you're telling us?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: That was only one day, but later when we came back from Ljubuski, then he took all 18 of us in a bus to Siroki Brijeg.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: All right. I think -- let me go back then to this interaction that you started to tell us about with Bosnjak. Now, can you go back -- if you can recall -- you're telling us about an exchange you have with Bosnjak and he taking you somewhere. Can you please state your answer again?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: Yes. Zeljko Bosnjak, when he came to the swimming pool, because I had worked at Zeljko's, and he knew where I was from. So he took me, and he took me to Tuta, and he said, "Boss, general, this is the mujahedin from Cazin."

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: And what else happened on that incident? Was anything else said or did anything else happen to you when he introduced you to Tuta?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: Tuta looked at me, and he said, "Take him back to work at the pool. The pool has to be finished." Those were the words. So I was taken back, and I continued to work there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Moving forward, was there another time when this same Bosnjak took you and some other prisoners to work at some place other than the swimming pool?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: Yes. He took me to his house, to his private house, to work there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: And approximately how long did you work at Mr. Bosnjak's house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: I worked at Zeljko's for about 15 days.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Could I ask the usher to show the witness Exhibit P49? Yes, if it can be placed on the ELMO, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: This is Zeljko Bosnjak.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: That is the man that you've been telling us about in your testimony now this -- well, now, this afternoon, and in connection with --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: -- this house where you worked?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Did this Bosnjak ever say anything to you, or did you come to learn, of any relationship or role that he had in connection with this person Tuta?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: Yes. He was a colonel in Tuta's army. He openly said that. He did not hide it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Well, when you say "openly said it," what did he say in that regard, as close as you can remember?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: Well, I remember when I went to work at his house, that he said, "I am Tuta's colonel, and you will work here." He had started building a new house, and I -- I am a professional in this line of work, and I worked a lot on this building.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: All right. Let me go forward. Apart from working at Bosnjak's house, did there come a time when this Ivan Cikota, whom you've already identified, came and took you to perform some work, or wanted to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: Yes. They quarrelled over who was going to take me to work for them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Was there another HVO soldier involved in that exchange or around that time? Let me rephrase that. I don't mean an exchange in terms of an exchange of prisoners, but during the conversation, when they were -- Mr. Cikota and Bosnjak were having words, was there another HVO soldier there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: There were soldiers there, but of the ones whom I knew was Juka Prazina, but they always had their bodyguards, they always had soldiers surrounding them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: All right. Well, what happened as a result of this -- these words between Cikota and Bosnjak? Did you go work for Cikota or did you go work for Bosnjak or somebody else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: At that time, I worked for both of them. I went two days to Zeljko's and then two days at Cikota's and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: During the time that you were working at Cikota's house, did you work there with any other prisoner that you've identified to us today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: Other work -- other soldiers worked. I can name them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, again, if we can go into private session for, I think, one question, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We will go to the private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: The transcript, Your Honour, is not correct on these names, and since the Prosecutor believes this to be important, we also believe it to be important, and we ask that they be cleared up. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think we have to go back to the private session to clear up those names.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We will go back to the private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We are now in the open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Now, around this time, were some of you moved from the MUP station to the tobacco station where you were held?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: We were all transferred to the tobacco station except for one prisoner who stayed behind. He wasn't with us at all. He was -- he didn't belong with our group. And the 18 of us were moved to the tobacco station.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: All right, Witness. About this person who stayed behind, I don't know which person you are about to name. I don't know. Do you think it's important? Is this a name that you feel is sensitive, or do you feel you can tell us that name without going into private session?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: No, I really don't know the name. I only know his last name was Batlak, that he was a HOS man. And that perhaps at the beginning of the war, he was wounded and his heel on one leg was missing. He was always wearing this black HOS suit.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Witness, I'm not going to pursue that further, then.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sorry. I forget to go back and forth. My apology.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: After you were being held then --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I'm sorry, can the usher show the witness, please, 26.9.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Looking at Exhibit 26.9, sir, is that -- when you say at the tobacco station, is that a photograph of the tobacco station where you were then held for some time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: Yes, there are bungalows of the tobacco station here in this row. We were in the first one next to the fence.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: All right. Well, Witness CC, I had not intended to really spend a lot of time on this at this point in the trial. But perhaps you can point out where you were, the building you just now identified.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: Maybe the first one next to the road to the fence here.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, I don't intend to spend extensive time identifying the location. I think, again, there comes a time. If counsel wants to, they can. But we don't intend to pursue this with every single witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Now, during this time, after being moved to the tobacco station, did you continue doing work from time to time for Bosnjak and Cikota?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: For a while, yes. I went to work for Zeljko, for Ivan. And at some point, that stopped.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: All right. Now, did there come a time when another -- someone you have mentioned already, an HVO officer -- come back on the scene, if you will, and want you to do something?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: I really don't understand you. In which period?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: After the time that you went back to the tobacco station, were you ever asked to join the HVO?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: Yes. I had an interview when I was working in -- at Ivan's. Juka came and offered me to join his men together with the other three who transferred under him.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Was any other HVO soldier involved in this same conversation, or perhaps another conversation about you joining the HVO? And who was that, if there was, and what did this person say to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: I don't think we're talking about the same thing. Juka Prazina asked me to join, and I refused. After that, Zeljko told me to join so that I would be able to get out.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: All right. That's what I'm talking about. What happened then? Tell us about this conversation with Zeljko. Is this Mr. Bosnjak again, Zeljko Bosnjak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: Yes, that's him.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: All right. Tell the Chamber that conversation.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: Well, there were various conversations I had with Zeljko regarding my release because I was working for him, and he insisted that I cross myself, that I would be released. He said, "Convert. I'll bring a priest, and we'll release you. You can go to Makarska." I didn't want to do that, because if I converted, perhaps I would be forced to put on an HVO uniform. I didn't do that eventually, but it had been offered.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Well, you said a moment ago -- and it may be apparent to most people in the courtroom, but just so the record is clear. You said he insisted that you cross yourself. What did you understand that to mean?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: Well, to change my faith, to change my name or to become a Croatian, to become a Jozo in order to be free, to convert. Whether that was something he meant seriously, I cannot know, but that's what he said.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: When you said just now Jozo, to become a Jozo, what does that mean?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: That means a change of name. He would bring a priest with a list for baptism and get me to change my name. That's what he said.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: All right. So just -- again, just to be clear, you're not saying that he actually -- or are you -- that he actually brought a priest there to you when you were being held or working at his house, or he was just saying that's what he would do if you would agree to it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: When he insisted to release me, he had already released one man and another man. And I was working for him, and he wanted to get me released, too. And since I refused to change my name, I don't remember that he actually brought a priest. He didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: All right. Now we're moving on, Witness CC. So not about those conversations, but can you tell the Chamber, please, during the time that you were being held at the tobacco station, did you ever see this person that you've previously identified in your testimony as Tuta?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: Yes, I did see him, particularly when I was at the canal, when we were working at the canal. I saw him also outside the tobacco station.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: All right. Before we go to the canal, can you just tell the Chamber approximately how many times you saw -- you believe you saw Tuta around the tobacco station?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: Well, I can't say exactly, more than once anyway. It may have been two or three times. I didn't, of course, make notes every time I saw someone. But I did look.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: All right. Let's go forward. You said then you became involved in digging something called a canal. Can you tell the Chamber about that, and perhaps describe a bit more what this was and the work you were doing.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: Well, we had to dig what we call a canal, water supply canal, an irrigation canal. And we started digging in the direction of the hill.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Were you ever told to what location this canal was being dug?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: Towards Tuta's house. I know because guards were also telling us that Tuta has no water, that water has to be supplied to him. And that canal was going in the direction of Tuta's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Could you see a location that was known to you or identified to you as Tuta's house when you were working on the canal?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: Yes, I could see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Approximately how far was it from the point -- the location where you were working on the canal?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: Perhaps 300 to 500 metres from the tip of the canal, from Tuta's house. But I saw when we were coming by bus, we passed even more closely to Tuta's house. I could see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Well, will you tell the Chamber a bit more. How did you know or come to know that that was Tuta's house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: Well, the guards told us, and Tuta himself would come to the canal to see how the works are progressing.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Do you recall approximately how many times Tuta himself came to the canal?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: I can't remember how many times he personally came. It wasn't the place or the time to make a record, but he did come several times.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Now, were you working on this canal by yourself, or were there other prisoners with you? And if I can move us hopefully forward a bit, did you come to know there were prisoners that were also working there from a place called the Dobrkovici school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: Well, when we just started working, we didn't know that they were from the Dobrkovici school. We found out later that there were prisoners in the school of Dobrkovici, and we drove by that school, we stopped by that school, and -- for other prisoners to get in, and then we would continue to the canal. So there were other prisoners. There were us, from the tobacco station, plus another six people from the Dobrkovici school, who had been brought from Heliodrom to help out.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Did you hear around that time that a prisoner at the Dobrkovici school had been killed, or did someone tell you that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: I did. I heard about it even before. I could see, while we were driving to work, a man being carried out. Ivan came to the police station and he wanted to beat us, and since he recognised us as people who were working for him, he said, "I wouldn't beat you." And on that occasion, he said, "We've just killed a man in Dobrkovici." Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: When you say, "Ivan, Ivan," who are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: Hrkac, Ivan Hrkac, nicknamed Cikota.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Did Cikota say anything more to you or to identify who it was who allegedly, quote, they had just killed at Dobrkovici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: We found out that the gentleman's name was Krilic when we got in touch with those other people who were working together with us at the canal, and then we found out that the executed man's name was Krilic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: I'm go to ask the usher, please, to show you Exhibit P33.2 through .5, so .2, .3, .4, .5.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: I recognise the school at Dobrkovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Can you point the school out to us, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Witness, on this occasion, since I'm not sure there has been quite as much evidence on this matter yet, I'm going to ask you to mark this photograph. So if you can be provided a marker, the location that you just pointed at a moment ago, can you identify, can you mark on that a number 1?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: All right. Very well. Will you look, please, then, at 33.3? And can you identify for us any location in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: I can point the school at Dobrkovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: In the interests of time, Mr. President, I'm just going to identify for the record the witness has identified a large building with a red roof immediately to the left of centre of the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Can you please look at Exhibit 33.4? Do you recognise that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: That's the Dobrkovici school.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, there is only one prominent building in that photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: And can you please look at Exhibit 33.5? And again, will you identify that, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: That is that same school in Dobrkovici. I know everything by the entrance, because we stopped there many times while people got on the bus.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Where would the bus typically stop to pick up prisoners from the Dobrkovici school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: Right next to the fence, as close as possible to the fence, so that people could get off as quickly as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: All right. I'm not sure it's a major point but, Witness, could you mark that location with perhaps the number 2?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I think only one other question about the school, just so the record is clear, the photographs that you've looked at in the last few minutes, is that what the school looked like in the summer of 1993? I mean the condition of the building, the paint, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: On the outside, yes. Maybe the roof has been changed since. There are new tiles and new varnish. But the frame is the same and the entrance is the same, as I could be looking at it right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: All right. Witness CC, moving forward, directing your attention to the early part of August 1993, did you have some meeting or communication with a man named Andabak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: Yes. I had communication. Once when he was taking us - I don't know exactly what the name of the mountain was, I'm not familiar with that area - on one occasion, when he took us to put up a cross.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: All right. Well, before you get to that --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter missed the last part of the answer. Would the witness please repeat?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Did you hear -- I'm sorry, Witness, did you hear the interpretation? They asked you to repeat the last part of your prior question about being taken to put up a cross.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: Once he came to the tobacco station, picked up several of us and took us to put up this cross. It was on a mountain. It was a huge cross. We needed to dig a hole, put up that cross, and pour concrete over it. It was personally Andabak who was in charge of this job. And the second time I saw Mr. Andabak when he came to the tobacco station. I was beaten on that occasion. And I saw Andabak then as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: All right. Well, on that occasion - I think that's the one I want to ask you about now - how did Andabak, if he did, identify himself? Did he describe himself with any rank?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: Yes. He introduced himself, he said, "I am Ivan Andabak, colonel of the Poskok Battalion, with Tuta. And Tuta's deputy." He used those words. He said, "I am Tuta's deputy."

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: How was Mr. Andabak dressed at that time, at the time you said he came to you at the tobacco station?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: I think he was wearing a uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: If the -- all right. Well, if the --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Just trying to decide whether to take the time, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: If the usher could please show you what's been marked as Exhibits P39.1, .2 and .3? Sorry --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I have 2 and 3. I have misplaced 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: That's all right. We will go with 2 and 3.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: Ivan Andabak.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: All right. Hold on one minute, Witness, let me catch up with you. So the record is clear --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: There is no microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: My apology. So the record is clear -- I can't see the exhibit number on that photograph, but Mr. Usher, can you help us with which photograph is that? The Exhibit number? So we are looking at 39.2. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Sir, and you told us that's the man what you came to know as Ivan Andabak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: That's how he introduced himself.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: All right. And I suppose, so the record is clear, there are two men in the photograph. Which one are you identifying as Andabak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can the witness be shown 39 -- I think you have them all now. Why don't we go back to 39.1.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Can you identify the person in the camouflage uniform, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: Ivan Andabak.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Thank you, Mr. Usher. That's fine. I'm not going to pursue the third photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Now, you said -- I think you said, if I heard you correctly, and if I'm wrong, please say so -- that it was around this time when you were seen by Andabak that you were beaten. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Tell us what happened, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: One day Ivan came together with another two men. I don't know who they were. I knew one nicknamed Bim. I knew him from when I was working someplace, and I didn't know the other one at all. All I know is they were accompanying him. The other one was Mario. The guard took us out from the room where we were sleeping and took me to see them. There was a reception booth at the entrance where we were locked in. They ordered me to sit on the table. And to one side of me, there was Bim, and to the other side, there was Mario.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: And what happened after that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: And then Ivan introduced himself. That's what he did before anything else, as I already mentioned. And then he started to question me. His first question, I remember well, was, "Do you know about the tunnel leading from Vranica underground to the left bank of East Mostar?" Meaning that there was a tunnel below Vranica leading to the left bank to East Mostar. I said I didn't know. If I had known, I wouldn't be there. And then the beating started.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Let me stop you there for a moment, because I think we'll have to finish this story after lunch.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: But just one question, Mr. President, if I can be allowed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: You said that Andabak identified himself, and I think you said something to the effect "as he always did." Did he always identify himself to you in the same way? And if so, again, can you tell the Chamber the words that he used to describe himself.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: He always introduced himself as a colonel. I think he was proud of that, and he was proud of being a deputy of Mladen Naletilic, Tuta.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, we can stop there, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Would you please inform this Trial Chamber how long you are going to take after the lunch break, because we hoped we could finish this witness today.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I hope so as well. Your Honour, it had been my goal, to be honest, to finish him before lunch. But I think it will be 10 minutes after the lunch break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We will resume at 3.00 this afternoon. --- Luncheon recess taken at 1.02 p.m. 19 20 21 22 23 24 25

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I'm very sorry about the delay for about 15 minutes. We might sit a little bit longer than we scheduled. Yes, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Witness CC, we left off before lunch, you had been in an interrogation involving Andabak, and I think, as you described it, two of his -- well, two of the soldiers were with him, one on each side of you, and sitting in front of -- you sitting in front of Andabak. And you said that one of the questions, one of the items that Andabak asked you about was some alleged tunnel out of the Vranica building. I think we've talked about that enough, but my question to you, then, is: Was there anything else that you were questioned about other than the tunnel?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: After a brief beating, the second round of questioning started with where was safe at the Vranica. I had no idea that there was some safe in the Vranica building or some money, and again, when I said that I did not know anything about it, the beating resumed. And then the question that followed were the ones that I could not even understand, and then I concluded that these were just a pretext for further beating, nothing else.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: And briefly, sir, how were you actually beaten? What did they do to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: There were kicks, there were punches, there were -- there was also handle of a pistol that they called a Zagja [phoen]. I don't know why they called it that. Then eventually they started trampling on top of me. After I was sent back to the cell, and there were traces of boots, there were imprints of boots all over me and they -- the prisoners made jokes, because they didn't have footwear, they said if they could borrow some of the boots that they saw the marks of on me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Of the people who were in the room at this time, who actually beat you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: I was beaten by the person nicknamed Bim. I know that he lived across the street from the MUP in Siroki Brijeg. I saw him. And Mario, nicknamed Robija, the two of them beat me, and Ivan Andabak gave orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: That was my question to you: Did Mr. Andabak or Colonel Andabak, did he physically touch you or was he just watching all this happen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: He only issued orders. He only watched and he did not touch me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Did he do anything to intervene or to stop the soldiers, the other two, from beating you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: How was he going to do that when he said, "Hit him, fuck his balija mother"? How do you mean did he stop them?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Now, let me direct your attention to another separate item. Were you ever taken to engage in looting or taking property out of houses or flats?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: Yes, I was taken to Mostar to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: And who took you, and what did you do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: The first time we went there, we looted for the soldiers who were in Siroki Brijeg, and Robo Medic was the one who drove us. They were looting furniture and things like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Did this Robo Medic have any role in the Convicts Battalion as far Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. as you know? Was he an officer? Did he have some position?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: Well, I think that he had some rank. He was a commander of recruits who were trained there at Siroki Brijeg.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us approximately how many times were you taken to Mostar to engage in looting in this way?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: I cannot say exactly. I cannot recall exactly, but more than twice definitely. Two, three times, because I was also taken to loot when that barracks in Mostar -- when that house was converted to the barracks, then they were going to put in furniture. And we worked there. This is where the recruits were training, and we had to bring that looted stuff from Mostar in order to appoint those premises.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Do you know what premises or what properties you looted, or how those properties were selected?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: Whatever was of good quality, sofas and TV sets, radio sets, refrigerators, stoves, rugs, if they were in good shape, good condition. They would fill the truck, so there were truckloads of stuff being hauled away.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: In terms of the flats or houses which were looted, can you tell the Chamber whether or not they were selected in any way on the basis of national group or ethnicity, that is whether the people or former owners or current owners or occupants were Croats, Serbs, or Muslim, or if it was just simply, if I can say, opportunistic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: No, those was were Muslim apartments and houses, the ones who had been expelled from their homes. Because we also saw some books in there, like the Koran or Musaf [phoen], so they had to have been Muslim homes. So I conclude that they were Muslim because they were abandoned, and Croats did not abandon houses in the western section of Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Witness, at some point, were you taken from the tobacco station to the Heliodrom where you were held at the Heliodrom for some time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: That was at the end of my stay at Siroki Brijeg. After that, I no longer went back to Siroki Brijeg.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Did you ever see a man named - may have been known to you, maybe not - as Vinko Martinovic or Stela at the Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: My apology.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Did you ever see a man perhaps known to you as either Stela or Vinko Martinovic at the Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: During the looting, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: At any time.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: I never knew who Stela was. I had never seen him. But at one point at the Heliodrom, the prisoners pointed him out to me. And they said that is Stela. That is how I saw him for the first time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Final topic, Witness CC: During the time that you were being held at various places that you've told us about today, did you ever see any soldiers or components of the army of the Republic of Croatia, that is, the HV?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: Yes, I did see them at Heliodrom and at Dretelj.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Can you describe or give us as much information as you recall about the HV personnel that you saw at the Heliodrom. Do you remember a name and just briefly what you saw?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: I know that they were at the Heliodrom, and there was a man of ours from -- who was brought from Siroki Brijeg, and he worked for the Croatian army. Apparently, they had beat him. And that night, he came back and sort of grabbed on to me, asking for some kind of support. He was all beaten up. He told me that they were Croatian army. And also, once when we were cleaning around the tarmac, we saw the Croatian army soldiers, we saw the patches.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Well, that was my next question to you: How did you come to know, or what do you base your testimony on, that these were HV soldiers or HV units?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: Based on the -- based on the patches. And also where they slept, above the door-frame, there was a large sign saying, "Croatian army."

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: All right. And you don't remember any of the names of these Croatian units this afternoon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: People who said -- spent more time at Heliodrom said that they were the Tigers, the Dragons, the Tigers. They said that all these units were there at the Heliodrom.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: And is it correct, sir, that you were finally released from custody on the 19th of March, 1994, after being held for a total of 314 days?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness CC. Mr. President, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any cross-examination? Yes, Mr. Krsnik? Cross-examined by Mr. Krsnik:

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, witness.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Let me introduce myself, I'm Kresimir Krsnik. I am the attorney for the accused Mladen Naletilic. I will ask you some questions. Please follow my questions carefully and I will try to frame them in such a way that you are able to answer very briefly and succinctly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would also like to ask that the ELMO be lowered. And, Your Honours, can we go immediately into the private session? Because I would like to ask several questions that need to be asked in the private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Go to the private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me, do you remember the statements that you gave earlier, before your evidence today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Do you remember how many statements you gave?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: No. I never counted them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Do you recall the statement you gave on -- that is to AID, the agency of -- Agency for Investigation and Documentation in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: I do, for the most part, yes, I do remember, and if we were to go in order, I think that I would be able to retell you everything that happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: And everything that you said to the AID people and the investigators of this Tribunal is the truth as you could recall it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: Whatever I could recall, I said in a truthful way.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Do you recall that in the first statement, of 8 April 1997 - that was the statement to the AID - you said that you were at the Vranica building and not in the logistics building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: No. That's not how I said it. I know that I was in the logistics building and that I crossed the roof to go into the Vranica building. If they wrote it differently, that's their matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: But it is possible that somebody also wrote down something that you did not say?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to answer that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Your statement to the AID starts as follows: "When the HVO launched its attack on 9 May, 1993, I was at the Vranica building, the building housing the command of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: No, unless they considered the entire complex the Vranica building, but I was in the logistics building.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Is it true that you crawled across the roof from the logistics building to the Vranica building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: Yes. We climbed up the logistics building. We -- and then we came out on to the roof, and we crawled over to the Vranica building.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Is it true that you entered the building through a hole made by a shell?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: Yes, because otherwise we would not have been able to enter it. There is some kind of a housing, and we wouldn't have been able to go in.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can we go into the private session for a second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We'll go to the private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: In the statement that you gave to both the AID and the statement you gave to the investigator on the 3rd of March, 1998, you -- in both statements you state the same: "We went on foot from the building to the school of mechanical engineering. In front of the faculty of mechanical engineering, I saw Tuta," and so on and so forth. And the same you stated to the investigators of the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: But that was not on the 8th. That was on the 10th. And what I Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. stated then, it was the truth, and I can state it again. I'm sorry. You said 8 March 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Sir, will you please listen very carefully. You gave your statement in the -- you gave a statement in March, and it was not in '93, but in '98. I was just referring to that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: On the 8th of March, I could not have given the statement because I was released on the 19th of March.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Witness, will you please focus and listen very carefully to my questions, please. I said 1998. So please follow the question very carefully. Thank you. However, in the statement that you gave to the AID and the statement that you gave to the investigator, you state emphatically that you were taken from the Vranica building to the school of mechanical engineering.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: Yes, I was taken there. In fact, I don't know whether this was the faculty of mechanical engineering school or some kind of a ministry. I am not from Mostar, but I know I was taken there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: In the statement you gave to the investigator, you say -- you stated clearly, We were taken to the ministry at Bijeli Brijeg in Mostar. Some people also refer to that place as the school of mechanical engineering, so you know very well where you were taken.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: Sir, I say to you again, I do not know Mostar. It could be that I said Bijeli Brijeg. I know that if I were to go there now, I would be able to tell you -- to show you the way, which way I was led. But I know exactly where I was taken from to the place where I was taken. And from that place, I was taken to Siroki Brijeg.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: So how did you know the names of these locations in your statements that you gave to both the AID and to the investigators of this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: The names of these locations, I heard from other prisoners about them. They refer to them. They named them. Some said one. Some named one. Some named another place, but I personally did not know their names.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: So what you said to the investigators of this Tribunal and to the AID is something that you heard from others in terms of the names of those locations?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I ask the usher, please, to place this map of Mostar in front of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Mr. Krsnik, what is the point of this cross-examination? We have had at least four witnesses who have described the walk from the Vranica building to this particular place. We have even seen it on video. So what is the point of getting all upset about whether he knows the right name or whether he told -- shouldn't we move on to what's important in this case? Unless you can tell me what the point of all this is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for your comments, Your Honour. Of course there is meaning to this, and I am prepared to tell you what it is if the witness is led out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Once it's relevant, go ahead. I didn't want to interrupt you. But it isn't as if it could possibly be in dispute that a number of prisoners walked for 10 to 20 minutes to a particular building, in front of which there were a number of people, one of whom was your client, and that certain incidents occurred. We have heard this from many witnesses. Now, I'm not going to disturb you if you say it's relevant, and I don't want you to explain. I'll have to trust you on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: By the way, Mr. Krsnik, would you please tell us the number about this map?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is Exhibit P11.18. Your Honour, Judge Clark, let me just remind you what the last witness said where he was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: I thought that most of the witnesses described a faculty building, whether it was mechanical engineering or the ministry. You don't agree? Well, then I won't interrupt, then.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This exhibit number is D1/28.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Witness, can you show this location on the map? Perhaps it will refresh your memory with names of streets?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: It was only then, I was then on that site for the only time. And I'm not really from Mostar. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Thank you. Thank you, usher.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: We heard your testimony today as to what happened in -- outside the building. Do you know that in your statement given to AID, you gave only one sentence about this and no more than that, namely that Tuta and Misic had an argument or quarrelled, that is Tuta, Misic, Lasic and the others, regarding the execution. However, Juka didn't allow it. But that's the only thing you said. There was not a word more about it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: That's the way it happened. Juka and Lasic defended us, saying that we should not be executed. And after that, we were taken to Siroki Brijeg, and Tuta used these words: "Go take them to Siroki Brijeg. Who said that balijas can't go to Listica? Go take them to Listica and execute them." Those were the words he used. So we didn't spend a long time outside the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: When you arrived outside the MUP building in Siroki Brijeg, do you stand by your claim as given today in your examination-in-chief? Do you know what you said in your previous statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: "Cane showed up, I don't know his first or last name. He was chief of the MUP. At that time, I didn't know it. However, during the time I spent in prison, he visited and it's from him that I heard that he was the chief. In addition, Cane knew Spahic from before, and we learned it from him."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Today, you said something entirely different. You said he knew Zekic and in addition Goran --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: I knew that because Zekic was at the police headquarters at the HVO up there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Witness, what is true, what you said today or what you said in your statements?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: It's all the truth. The Prosecutor didn't ask me about Spahic. Perhaps he didn't know to ask me but it's true that he knew both Goran and Spahic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Witness, tell me how many times Romeo Blazevic came to your cell?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: As far as I know, he came once.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: And never again?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: As far as I know, he didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: How many times Cikota came?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: I didn't count. He came a lot of times. I really didn't count. Cikota came often to the cells and to the tobacco station, but I didn't count his visits.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: In your statement, you mention only one incident, namely in the canteen of the MUP, and nothing else.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: I wouldn't agree with that. Perhaps I mentioned something but I don't believe I said that. He did come.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Witness, did you have enough food and water, both in prison and while you were working at the pool?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: I know I got out weighing 40 kilos. I know how much food and water I had. No, there wasn't. At no time were we really washed. We were never allowed to have a bath.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: In your statement, or rather statements, that you gave and which I can present to you, if you like, you said, "I remember that we got enough food and water."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: I don't remember that statement. You can let me see it, but I really don't remember. As far as I know, I never said we had enough food and water. Especially water, because in -- during the entire time we spent there, we were never allowed to have a bath, to wash ourselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With the usher's assistance, I would like to show this witness his own statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: That's the statement you gave to the investigators of this Tribunal. Have you read it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Did you say that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: Yes, I did, but what I was referring to was a private person who brought us food, and we know exactly who paid for it and who brought it to us. It was the housekeeper in Siroki Brijeg, a man named Tomo.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Did you also get enough cigarettes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: Cigarettes? Yes, I smoked. I smoked leaves, if I could gather some. If you did work for private persons, you got rewarded sometimes, but there was nothing regular. Nothing was regular there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: You said today that you were guarded by drivers. Do you stand by that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: Yes, drivers wearing uniforms, armed, yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: In your statements, you said that you were guarded by 25 young soldiers who had been trained by Robo Medic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: At the tobacco station, yes, we were guarded by them. I am not saying there were 25, but we were guarded by such recruits, and when we were building the barracks, they guarded us. We were also guarded by home guards. At least that's what they called themselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Witness, you expressly said, "I used to see him on Siroki Brijeg. He trained about -- he trained about 25 young recruits, who later guarded us around the swimming pool -- at the swimming pool."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: I certainly gave no such statement, because the barracks were built after the swimming pool.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With the usher's assistance, I would like to show this statement to the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can the counsel be advised to give at least references of the passages that are being read and quoted so that the interpreters can follow. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik. Did you hear what the interpreters said? The interpreter said that could the interpreters be provided the reference of the passages that are being read and quoted so that the interpreters can follow your questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a statement dated 8th of April, 1997 given to the Agency for Investigations and Documentation, page 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Did you read this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Did you say that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: Perhaps I said something like that, but not this. Of course, I said I saw Robo Medic, but I really can't remember saying that he guarded us around the swimming pool.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Will you tell me, then, do you stand by your statement that around the canal which you dug for the purposes of irrigation --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: Water supply.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Water supply, from that point, you can see Mr. Naletilic's house.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Exhibit --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters didn't get the number.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Exhibit 26.2, Prosecutor's Exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [In English] 26.2.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Witness, kindly look at this aerial photograph. Do you see the swimming pool? You can take the photograph and look at it more closely. Perhaps the image on the screen isn't very good.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: I said I could see Tuta's house from the canal, not from the pool.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you now, do you see the swimming pool? I know exactly what I'm asking.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Now, let us move towards this canal. Move the pointer, please, to this canal, going from the swimming pool.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: I think you could have taken a better picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: We'll have to do with what we've got.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: This is sheer camouflage.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Do you see your canal on this picture?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: Around here, but I can't be sure because the picture is really terrible. But I think it's here.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Will you show it on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: Around here. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Will you make a dot on this picture and mark it with number 1.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: I'm really not sure, because of the quality of the picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: And can you trace the path of this canal?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: I can't.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: If you can't, just put this number 1 on the picture.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: I don't really understand this picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: No problem. Just put the number 1.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: Make a better picture. I know this house very well. I saw it many times from the bus, and what you are showing me here --

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: You saw Tuta's house from the bus?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: All right. Tell me, please, you mentioned today that Eldar Omerika was together with you at the pool and helping you out with the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: No, it wasn't Eldar that I mentioned. Eldar was killed at the logistics building. I mentioned Armin.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: We can look at the transcript. We can rewind the transcript. You said Eldar Omerika.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: I want to ask you: Eldar Omerika, was this man with you or wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: You mean Armin Omerika.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Armin. If you can just give me a second, please. So it was Armin Omerika who was with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: When you mentioned Omerika, you mean Armin?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: And not Eldar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: Regrettably, not Eldar. Eldar got killed in the logistics building on the first day of the conflict.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Did HOS attack the Vranica building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: I don't know if it was HOS, but there were individuals in black uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: I will show you again your statement in which you said, when you were crawling up to the window on the first floor --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: "I saw HVO soldiers shooting from the barracks. They were in HOS uniforms, black shirts, black trousers, HOS patches on their sleeves. Some had helmets on their heads. Some had stockings. Some had nothing at all." Do you want to read this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: There is no need to.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Did you say this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: Perhaps not exactly like that. Perhaps I didn't mean that. But something to that effect. Civilian police also fired from the prison -- or from the shelter.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, it was probably from the shelter, from shelter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Do you remember saying today that Mr. Jahic was forced to sign some sort of statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: You said it was before you went to Ljubuski?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: Exactly on the day when we started for Ljubuski.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: You say in your statement -- you say expressly that it was the HVO civilian police who came to the prison when you had already returned from Ljubuski - I won't read this from the beginning - and it was then that Hamdija Jahic had to sign a paper stating that the behaviour of the guards in the prison was correct and that detainees were not mistreated. Today, you spoke of the Geneva Convention. Do you want to read this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: What I said today is true. Whether anyone added something to my statement, I don't know, and I don't care, but I stand by what I said today. On the day that we left for Ljubuski, yes, the civilian police came, they took away Hamdija, and Hamdija had to sign this. But the civilian police did not drive us away. It was soldiers who drove us to Ljubuski.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: You said a moment ago it's possible that the AID added something to your statement.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know. I can't say exactly what happened on each day out of 314 days. You should know better.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Witness, but you said a moment ago yourself, "I don't know if AID added something."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: I can't remember every word that I stated seven or eight years ago. Please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Witness, we understand that you're eager to give your testimony, but you have also to remember that you're under the protective measures. So please wait until the Defence counsel finished his question. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, while we are -- while you've intervened I'm going to raise the question, object to the procedure. We are back to the same problem we've had before. Mr. Krsnik has now gone on for some time, and I have not intervened, well, to give him some latitude, but put the document -- the document should be put in front of the witness. There has been extensive examination on these documents, and once again they have not been put in front of the witness. Now, we've gone over this again and again and again. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I quite agree with you. And Mr. Krsnik, we have already mentioned that. If you want to use a document, better put this document, especially the previous statement, to this witness. We should be fair to this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course, Your Honour. That's exactly what I'm doing. What I was going to say, I want to make my cross-examination brief. There are certain statements that can be taken out of context, if you followed, and of course you followed, my cross-examination. There is one statement made to the investigators, one statement made to the agency, one completely different statement today. The whole text does not have to be reread. What is at issue are particular, separate statements, and it is especially relevant when we have other witnesses speaking to the same circumstances. We are entitled to determine whether their testimony -- whether the information they provide differs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Whether there are discrepancies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I understand your reasoning, but to be fair to this witness, you have to put that statement to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Certainly, Your Honour. While my colleague is looking for this particular passage -- Mr. Usher, if you would be so kind?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Please look at the section which is underlined.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Could we have a reference, Your Honour, so we can follow?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, yes, Mr. Krsnik? Could you give us some guidance? Page 5, given -- in the statement given to the investigators, that's to say, page 5 in the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: This, sir, is precisely what I've referred to. Several days later, that is, after we left Siroki Brijeg.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Did you ever see the person you referred to as Andabak on television?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: On television? I don't remember. Maybe, maybe not. Why would I have to see him on television?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Because you stated that you had seen him on television.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: I remember saying that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: So it wasn't really a problem recognising him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: It will never be a problem to recognise him. I remember him so well that I will never have a problem recognising him. That's what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would now like Exhibit 26.9 to be shown.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Kindly show us where you slept, or where you were accommodated on this photograph.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: The tobacco station.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Use the pointer, please, if you could be so kind as to show us where you slept.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: These buildings are the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: So, we can identify this as the building with the grey roof behind the building with the red roof, third building from the pool. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, would you please tell me who guarded you and who did this building belong to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: I can tell you who guarded us; but who the building belonged to, I don't know. All they said was tobacco station. How would I know who owned the building? The place where we slept also accommodated the Poskok Battalion, and we were guarded by HVO guards. That would be all.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Do you know what is the connection between Poskok Battalion with the Convicts Battalion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: I have no clue. Nobody told us anything. How would I know if there is any connection or what it is? But it must be the same thing. These people bragged of being members of the Convicts Battalion, and at that place, it was written Poskok Battalion. Maybe it's not the same, but to me it's the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: One final question: Would you be able to point for us on the map the way you went to loot, who went with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: You could show it on the map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: No, I couldn't. I already told you I don't know Mostar. I don't know the place at all. I only know the area where I live and nothing else. But I can tell you the names of people who went with us, who accompanied me. Maybe not all the names.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: So who were the soldiers who were -- accompanied you to that looting expedition? You said Robo Medic. Maybe someone else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: Maybe I could remember some other people. I remember Robo the best because he was around the most.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My colleagues pointed out that I missed something.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: You said that Tuta was referred to by some as "General" and by some others as "Boss" or "Chief". Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: He was referred to everywhere, or was it at the pool, in front of the ministry? Can you be specific.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: Today, I said when Zeljko took me to Tuta, he said, "General." And when I worked, they referred to him both "General" and "Boss." But I remember very well at the pool side when he took me there personally, that is what was said.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: You said -- do you know that you never said anywhere except today that Andabak said, "Hit the balija"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: Yes, you just reminded me today. In fact, you sort of provoke me into remembering certain things.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me, do you know that you never said that anybody referred to you as a mujahedin except today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: I may have omitted it but I know very well that that is what Zeljko said at that time. I think that Mr. Naletilic probably remembers that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: And do you know what you stated to both the investigators and to the AID?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: Yes, for the most part, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Did you tell them about the mujahedin?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: Maybe yes, maybe no. I have been trying to forget, sir. It's been eight, nine years, I wish to somehow get it out of me, to -- but some things come back, some things I may omit. All these are details. But the things that happened did happen this way, and that's the whole truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, sir. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Seric, any cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we have no reason to cross-examine this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any re-examination, Mr. Scott?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I think I've going to have about two questions, Your Honour. If I could just have a minute, though, please? Excuse me, Your Honour, maybe Mr. Poriouvaev can help me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President, I've now found the reference in the English version, but now I have to find it -- well if I can have the usher's assistance. Re-examined by Mr. Scott:

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Witness CC, if you can find the statement that Mr. Krsnik was just asking you about -- I can't help you very much, I'm afraid, with the B/C/S version, but if you can find page 6, and it's the part where you -- the statement about your conversation with Mr. Zeljko Bosnjak about his introducing you to Tuta, if you can find that. It may -- in the English version, it's at the top of page 7. It may be either at the bottom of page 6 of the B/C/S version or somewhere around there. Just so I know we are looking for the same thing, are you looking for the passage concerning when Zeljko Bosnjak introduced you to Tuta? Do you know what we are looking for?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: "He called Tuta over and he said, 'This balija came from Cazin to fight in Mostar.' Tuta listened and did not say anything, so I continued working."

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: So the record is clear, I've just referred you to your statement Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. to the OTP investigators dated the 3rd of March, 1998, and as recorded in your statement, did you say that Zeljko Bosnjak called Tuta and told him, "This balija came from Cazin to fight in Mostar"? Is that what it says in your statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: It is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: So if I understand your testimony, sir, the only difference between what you said today and what you said in your statement of 1998 is today you used the word "mujahedin," and in 1998, the word that was used to refer to you was "balija," but do you remember that account? Do you remember this happening?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CC
utterances.text: It's the same situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: And the last item -- or the last questions I'll put to you --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If the usher could assist by showing the witness Exhibit 25.2, which is -- you can put that on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Witness CC, can you look at that photograph, please, and, if you can, can you see any place on that -- depicted on that photograph where you were working on this canal, or a reservoir that was connected to the canal, or a well?
